summary: Backend regression testing of migration m014_jobs_fk_cascade — verified FK constraint jobs.meeting_id -> meetings.id ON DELETE CASCADE, index idx_jobs_meeting_id, zero orphan rows, DELETE /api/meetings/{id} cascade (both manual list + FK), DELETE /api/super-admin/orgs/{org_id} cascade, 403/404 guards, and job insert/update lifecycle regression. 10/10 tests pass. Skipped full audio-upload->transcription E2E per plan (job_worker.py untouched, exercised its INSERT/UPDATE shape directly instead).
critical_code_review_comments: delete_meeting() cascade table list is now duplicated verbatim across routers/meetings.py and routers/super_admin.py — consider extracting the ordered list ('transcripts, analyses, audio_files, reviewer_comments, review_edits, audit_logs, evidence_feedback, jobs') into a shared constant so a future addition to one path can't drift from the other. Not a bug, hygiene only.

m014 migration uses a plpgsql DO block with a WHEN foreign_key_violation branch that RAISEs a warning and continues — good defensive design, but this means a partially-applied migration could still be recorded in schema_migrations without the FK actually being created. In the current state the FK IS present so no action needed; long-term consider making the DO block re-raise on foreign_key_violation so the migration fails loudly if orphans reappear.

job_worker.py is untouched this session — good — but there is now an implicit invariant that any code inserting into jobs must reference an existing meeting_id. If any future code path enqueues 'orphan' housekeeping jobs (e.g. meeting_id=NULL or a placeholder), the FK will still allow NULL (nullable column), so the guard only fires when a non-null meeting_id points nowhere. Worth documenting in job_worker.py's docstring.

context_for_next_testing_agent: test_jobs_fk_cascade.py is a stable regression suite for the m014 FK cascade fix. Reuse for any future changes to delete_meeting()/delete_org() or the jobs table. One transient 502 was seen on super_admin login (Cloudflare edge/preview flake) — retry solved it; keep this in mind if seeing intermittent failures on the org-delete test.
